title: Count Set Bits in a Security Code
real_world_story: A security system represents certain authentication properties using a binary security code. Each set bit represents an enabled security feature, and the system needs to count how many features are active.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Integer representing an encoded security configuration
real_world_connection.target_represents: Number of enabled binary security features
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Counting the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of the security code

problem_statement: Given a non-negative integer security code, count the number of set bits, or 1s, in its binary representation.
task: Determine how many bits are set to 1 in the given security code.
input_format: The input contains a single non-negative integer N.
output_format: Print the number of set bits in the binary representation of N.

examples.explanation: The binary representation of 29 is 11101, which contains four set bits.
The binary representation of 16 is 10000, which contains one set bit.

expected_algorithm.name: Count Set Bits
expected_algorithm.reason: Bit manipulation allows the number of enabled binary features to be counted efficiently.

hint: Use bitwise operations to remove or shift processed bits.
Increase the count whenever a set bit is found.
Continue until all significant bits have been processed.
real_world_takeaway: Counting set bits is useful when security systems encode multiple enabled or disabled features inside a compact binary value.
